Genre: Exploring Identity, Global Citizenship, Inclusion, Storytelling, Wellbeing
Description: A flexible 4- or 8-week program for Years 7-8, ICAP builds cultural awareness, empathy, and self-esteem through interactive, facilitated sessions. Students explore identity, belonging, intersectionality, and global citizenship while fostering inclusive classrooms. Schools also receive a free Atlas membership, giving students access to interactive analytics that showcase their school’s cultural diversity—supporting learning across ICAP and the Modern Global Parliament. Program Outline 1. Welcome to ICAP – Co-create behaviour agreements, spark curiosity, and celebrate diversity. 2. Identity – Explore heritage and uncover hidden cultural layers. 3. Empathy & Belonging – Reflect on inclusion through games and scenarios. 4. Self-Esteem – Identify values and build emotional intelligence. 5. Intersectionality – Use Cultural Infusion’s Atlas to challenge stereotypes and celebrate diversity. 6. Create a World – Design unique cultures, fostering creativity and teamwork. 7. Interfaith Insights – Engage with interfaith presenters to broaden perspectives. 8. Model World Parliament – Apply intercultural skills in a mock global forum. Pricing $4,000 (eight × 90-minute sessions) **Fully government-funded for government schools in VIC**

Program_Name: Buddhist Chanting and Mindfulness Through Song
Description: Through this interactive workshop, students are introduced to the role of chanting and song in Buddhist traditions and how these practices cultivate mindfulness, compassion, and wellbeing. Melanie performs traditional chants and songs before guiding students to try simple chants together and even co-create their own based on values such as kindness and respect. Alongside the music, students learn about the Buddha’s teachings and their contemporary relevance to wellbeing and community.

Program_Name: Rhythms and Movements of Newar Culture
Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Experience the vibrant sounds and dynamic rhythms of Newar culture through a lively workshop that combines traditional music and dance from Nepal. Participants will be introduced to the dhime, a powerful twin-headed drum used in rituals and celebrations; the bansuri, a soothing bamboo flute known for its melodic tones; and traditional Newari dance, rich in storytelling and cultural symbolism. This interactive session includes live performance, cultural background and hands-on participation, giving everyone a chance to experience rhythms and movements.

Rubbing is perhaps one of the oldest techniques in printmaking. Created by carefully pressing paper onto a carved or textured surface, this traditional technique is used to copy designs and texts from stone, metal or wood. Believed to be originated in East Asia and practised in China as early as nearly 2,000 years ago, rubbing was primarily used for reproducing ancient inscriptions, calligraphy and relief carvings, preserving artworks and histories. Let’s explore the cultural and historical significance behind this intriguing technique by making some rubbing art together to appreciate the beauty of Chinese artwork in this hands-on workshop!

Program_Name: The Dragon and the Chinese Zodiac
Description: The story of the 12 Chinese Zodiac animals has a long and rich history, with every person having their own Zodiac sign based on their birth year. Among those 12 animals, the Chinese dragon stands out as a mystical, powerful creature that exists in imagination only, yet can be found everywhere within Chinese culture, from legends to idioms, and even to art! Representing power, benevolence and good fortune, dragons are deeply rooted in the Chinese culture. In this workshop, explore how dragons continue to inspire joy through dragon dance demonstrations, crafts-making, and storytelling about the Zodiac animals.

Program_Name: Chinese Wushu and the Monkey King
Description: Chinese martial arts, also known as wushu, consists of the rich tradition of combat techniques, philosophy, and health practices that developed over more than 4,000 years. Wushu embodies the harmony of Yin and Yang and promotes the Martial Virtues, such as humility, integrity, respect, and discipline. In this workshop, students will enjoy a dynamic demonstration and interactive practice session involving Taichi (Taiji) and ancient sword skills. They’ll also meet the beloved Monkey King from the classic tale of ‘Journey to the West’ and see how he learns wushu on his path to becoming a legendary hero! *Schools have the option to enhance this experience by booking an additional session of Chinese Shadow Puppetry, where the story of ‘Journey of the West’ will be brought to life through puppetry!

Program_Name: Ghana Road Show – For a limited time only!
Genre: Dance, Inclusion, Music, Storytelling, Theatre, Visual Arts
Description: Bring a piece of Ghana to your school and give your students a unique opportunity to learn about the rich Ghanaian cultural heritage from this dynamic live performance workshop! Students will be introduced to traditional West African acrobatics, circus skills, music and storytelling, and build physical confidence and teamwork through hands-on activities such as group balance, ball juggling and pan spinning! Featuring acclaimed artists from Ghana, juggler and circus performer Mutala, dancer and circus performer Adjei, as well as Lucky, a Ghana-born dancer and percussionist based in Sydney, the students will surely enjoy the vibrant energy of West Africa in this interactive workshop. Book fast, as this workshop is available exclusively in August and September 2025!

Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, SA, VIC, Virtual, WA
Genre: Exploring Identity, Global Citizenship, Inclusion, Wellbeing
Region: Africa, Asia, Europe, Middle East, Multicultural, North America, South America
Description: Bring your school’s cultural story to life! Imagine showing your students just how diverse and unique your school community really is. The Cultural Infusion Atlas for Schools is a world-first program that uses interactive data and vibrant visualisations to help schools explore, celebrate, and learn from their own diversity. Already used by leading organisations worldwide — from Carers Victoria to Amazon Web Services — this powerful tool is now available for schools. Why schools love the Atlas ✔️ Celebrates diversity – Students see their own identities represented and learn about those around them. ✔️ Promotes global citizenship – Aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goal 4.7, helping students build skills to thrive in a multicultural world. ✔️ Curriculum-ready – Comes with lesson plans and activities that bring the data to life in the classroom. ✔️ Exclusive recognition – Earn your school’s “Mapped & Measured” badge to showcase your commitment to inclusion. ✔️ Extra resources – Get free access to our Learning Lands platform, packed with cultural education materials. How it works Students and staff complete a quick, secure survey. Your school receives real-time, interactive insights showing the languages, cultures, and traditions that make your community unique. Teachers use the ready-to-go lesson plans to spark conversations and build intercultural understanding across year levels. Get involved 🎓 Pilot Program (FREE, limited spots, Term 4 2025) Be among the first schools in Australia to experience this groundbreaking program. 📅 General Access (Term 1 2026 onwards) Available to schools nationwide. 👉 Apply now to secure your place!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Maloya is a traditional Creole music and dance form originating from Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean. It was born out of the cultural heritage of African, Malagasy, and Indian indentured labourers brought to the island, often as an expression of resilience and a means of storytelling. The genre features rhythmic beats, call-and-response singing, and expressive dance, involving instruments such as the roulèr (bass drum), kayamb (a shaker made from sugar cane and seeds), and pikèr (bamboo). This workshop is designed to immerse participants in the cultural richness of Maloya, with activities adapted for different age groups.

Genre: Martial Arts, Music, Storytelling, Visual Arts
Description: This engaging workshop takes participants on a musical journey through China, exploring customs such as Tai Chi, calligraphy, and storytelling. Led by Ting, a classically trained musician and performer, the session features fascinating ancient instruments including the Chinese mouth organ, hulisi, flute, fiddle, lute, and percussion such as drums, gongs, and cymbals. Students will hear the unique sounds of each instrument while learning about the diversity and history of Chinese culture.

Program_Name: Journey Through Zimbabwe with Rumb Bee
Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Step into the world of Rumb Bee, a vibrant contemporary jazz artist, as she leads an immersive workshop that blends vocal expression, dance, and the entrancing sounds of the mbira (thumb piano). More than just a music session, this workshop is a celebration of identity, resilience, and the power of sound to connect across cultures. Through storytelling and song, Rumb Bee shares her personal journey- migrating to Australia, rebuilding from the ground up, and finding healing through music. Participants will learn the fundamentals of vocal control, expressive movement, and traditional rhythms from her homeland, all while gaining insight into how music can be a tool for emotional expression and cultural connection. Ideal for aspiring performers, music lovers, and curious minds of all ages, Rhythms of Resilience invites you to sing, move, listen and feel. Come ready to create, reflect, and be inspired by a story of courage, love, and the universal language of music.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Melanesian Infusion is a captivating workshop led by Natty, a talented musician and performer hailing from the Lau Tribe in Malaita Island Province, Solomon Islands. In this program, Natty shares the rich cultural heritage of the Solomon Islands tribes, offering participants a deep dive into the world of tribal songs, chants, and instruments. As a master of log drumming and a warrior of his people’s musical traditions, Natty invites you to explore the rhythms and stories that have been passed down through generations. This unique workshop is a celebration of Melanesian culture, blending music, storytelling, and spirituality in a way that connects the past with the present. Natty is touring Australia for a limited time.

In Rhythms of Latin America participants are introduced to the rich dance and cultural traditions of Hispanic countries through storytelling, movement and music. The program features a range of street Latin dance styles, introducing participants to the fun and upbeat rhythms of Salsa, Cumbia, Merengue, Samba and Tango. Each session begins by exploring the cultural context of a Latin American country through a short story, followed by easy-to-learn choreography inspired by both traditional and contemporary Latin music. The program encourages creativity, connection and a deeper understanding of storytelling through movement.

Program_Name: Rhythms and Jazz Across South and Central Africa
Description: Immerse yourself in the rich sounds of Africa with two distinct musical experiences. Choose between: Central African Grooves – A dynamic blend of classic and contemporary music from the Congo, Mozambique, and Kenya. This performance brings the infectious rhythms of the 1960s and ’70s into the present, featuring soulful melodies and energetic beats that showcase the region’s musical evolution. GDB Quartet – A South African jazz ensemble performing original compositions and timeless classics. With a lineup of piano, guitar, bass, and drums, they capture the spirit of South African jazz, from township swing to modern interpretations. Whether you prefer the pulsating rhythms of Central Africa or the smooth, expressive sounds of South African jazz, each performance offers a unique and unforgettable musical journey.

Program_Name: Roots & Rhythms: Embracing Heritage Through Performance
Description: Step into a vibrant fusion of Greek heritage, jazz, soul, and storytelling in this dynamic workshop led by seasoned performers, educators, and creative entrepreneurs, Mel and Kat. Through music, personal narratives, and interactive discussions, they inspire participants to harness their cultural roots, build confidence, and embrace creativity.With a selection of engaging focus topics, participants can explore: From Greek Cafés to Main Stages: A journey of creative entrepreneurship Cultural Roots, Lasting Confidence: Using heritage to strengthen identity Finding Your Voice: From shy kids to confident performers Empowered Storytelling: Sharing your heritage through narrative Community & Creativity: Building meaningful connections through the arts The Courage to Create: Pursuing passion and purpose as an entrepreneur Perfect for schools, community groups, and creative spaces, this workshop is an inspiring blend of tradition and modern artistry, designed to empower and connect.

This program offers students the opportunity to engage in the creation of an Aboriginal-inspired mural, working closely with an Aboriginal artist from start to finish. The project fosters cultural understanding, teamwork, and creative expression, while honoring the traditions of Aboriginal art. The journey begins with a Yarning Circle, where students gather to discuss and decide on the storyline that will form the foundation of the mural. In this circle, guided by the Aboriginal artist, students share ideas, learn about Aboriginal culture, and collaboratively develop a meaningful narrative for the artwork. Once the theme is established, students will work directly with the artist to bring the mural to life. A protective sealer will be applied to ensure the mural’s longevity. Painted on a canvas for easy display, the mural will be showcased in an office or public space, with all participants retaining the copyright of the artwork. A Certificate of Completion will be awarded, acknowledging your role in the creation of this cultural piece. Finally, the Yarning Circle will reconvene at the project’s conclusion, where students will reflect on their experiences and hand over ownership of the completed mural, celebrating their collective achievement.

Embark on an unforgettable cultural adventure with our “Journey Through Kenya” workshop, where students explore the vibrant traditions, stories, and celebrations of Kenya. This workshop can focus on one of the following topics, depending on your preferences: Cultural Tribal Dance: Students will learn traditional Kenyan dances, discovering the stories and rhythms behind each movement. Art & Craft Creation: Students will create their own Kenyan-inspired crafts while learning the cultural significance behind various designs and materials. Show and Tell: Through a display of Kenyan artifacts, students will engage with cultural items and hear their meaningful stories. Language Fun: Students will learn keywords and phrases in Swahili or local tribal languages to connect with the culture on a deeper level. Rites of Passage & Traditions: Students will hear stories about significant rites of passage and traditions that shape Kenyan communities. Kenyan Celebrations: Students will discover how Kenyan festivals and national holidays celebrate history, culture, and community. Cultural Fashion & Expression: Students will explore the colourful world of Kenyan fashion and learn how clothing expresses cultural identity and values.

Immerse students in the rich cultural traditions of Sweden with this engaging and interactive workshop, available for all age groups. Led by Rebecca, an accomplished Nyckelharpa player, the workshop celebrates Swedish heritage through music, dance, and storytelling. Participants will explore iconic Swedish folk music, including songs like the playful ‘Små Grodorna’ (The Small Frogs) and lively traditional dances such as the Polska and Halling. The program invites participants to sing, dance, and stomp along while learning about Swedish instruments like the Nyckelharpa, as well as the cultural significance of traditions such as Midsummer. Tailored to suit the age group, this workshop can engage younger children through simple songs and circle dances or offer deeper insights into Swedish folk music for older audiences.

This program will take you on a journey through the rich culture and history of the Māori people. This program will allow you to experience a range of traditional cultural customs including Kapa Haka (Māori performing arts), Taonga Puoro (Māori musical instruments) and Toi Māori (Creative Māori Arts). This program aims to foster new learnings, experiences and relationships through Māori ways of being, doing and living. Nau mai haere mai!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Immerse students in the culture of Colombia’s northern Caribbean coast, exploring its traditions and rhythms. Through dynamic styles such as Cumbia, Mapalé, La Puya, and Bullerengue, students will experience the unique sounds of the region. In this interactive workshop, participants will use their own bodies as instruments, recreating the rhythms of the Caribbean while learning about its diverse culture.

In this workshop, you will experience the enchanting sounds of traditional Thai Fiddle like the Saw Duang and Saw U, Bamboo Shaker and Thai Hammered Dulcimer, paired with the grace and beauty of Thai classical dance. Discover the stories behind Thailand’s rich musical heritage, learn the basics of playing traditional instruments, and explore elegant dance movements that reflect the harmony and rhythm of Thai life. Our presenter’s interactive and engaging sessions bring Thai culture to life, offering a unique opportunity to explore its artistic and spiritual roots.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: In Yalla! Arab Dance and Culture, participants will embark on a lively and engaging journey into the diverse and rich traditions of the Arab world. This highly interactive program offers an opportunity to explore Arab cultures and histories through dance, music, and storytelling. The Arab world is home to a variety of traditions, cultures, and dialects. This program celebrates this diversity, featuring presenters from Lebanon, Palestine, Syria, and beyond, and allowing participants to discover the beauty of cultural expressions that span regions and generations. One of the highlights of the workshop will be learning Dabke, the energetic and communal folk dance beloved in many Arab countries. Participants will have the chance to dance together, creating a sense of connection and joy as they experience the rhythm of the dance.

Step into the vibrant world of Henna art, a timeless tradition that weaves together history, culture, and creativity. In this 1.5-hour workshop, students will not only learn the rich cultural background of Henna, tracing its origins through Africa, India, and the Middle East, but they will also get a hands-on experience in creating beautiful Henna designs themselves.

This program is an immersive and interactive experience designed to ignite creativity, curiosity, and wonder in participants of all ages. Rooted in diverse cultural traditions from around the world, the program blends storytelling, performing arts, and visual arts to explore magical elements, folklore, and imaginative thinking. Participants are taken on a journey through captivating narratives, hands-on activities, and live performances that showcase the power of imagination in shaping cultures and communities.

In this exciting workshop, students will explore all things K-pop! This workshop will start with a skilled performance by our presenters, followed by a lesson on popular K-pop dance moves including the ‘Bang Bang Bang’ and ‘Mic Drop’. At the end of the workshop, students will have an opportunity to showcase their new dance skills to the popular K-pop sensation, Gangnam Style!

As part of the cherished tradition of the Moon Cake Festival, participants will be invited to decorate Chinese lanterns adorned with traditional patterns. These lanterns, often illuminated and displayed during the festival, are important symbols of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. Decorating the lanterns not only connects participants with the cultural significance of the festival but also allows them to engage creatively in this age-old celebration.

Dive into the world of origami with our Art of Origami workshop! This hands-on session will teach the Japanese art and science of paper folding, fostering creativity, concentration, and cultural appreciation. Participants will learn to create intricate designs while exploring the history and cultural significance of origami in Japan. Join us to unfold your potential and discover the magic of transforming simple paper into beautiful creations.

Program_Name: What It Takes to Get a Guinness World Record?
Description: Unique to Cultural Infusion – Guinness world record holder and coach Dean presents the inside world of Guinness. It begins with GWR history in the 1950’s when Guinness Brewery Director Sir Hugh Beaver had the idea to compile a book of facts and figures to promote Guinness beer. It explores what it takes to get a Guinness world record, details Dean’s personal Guinness story of hanging out with other world record holders -including the world champion toe wrestler, sitting the world’s smallest man on his knee, and shaking the world’s biggest hand. The talk includes some action film, archival photos, live demonstrations and interactive exercises that include giving students a chance to break an unofficial world record.

Japanese martial arts, traditionally known as budō (武道), are art forms that have evolved over centuries in Japan. In this high-energy educational workshop, participants will explore the rich history and philosophy of martial arts in Japan and have the opportunity to try various styles such as Karate, Judo, and Aikido. Translated as “the way of the warrior,” budō encompasses disciplines that require dedication, hard work, and practice. These concepts are of cultural significance and form the foundation of many Japanese martial arts. Adaptable to different ages and physical abilities, participants will gain an appreciation for the discipline, practice, and mastery that Japanese martial arts are renowned for.

Inspired by the farmers’ dance of China’s Korean ethnic group, Chinese Korean Ethnic Dance offers a dynamic blend of tradition and expression. Through rhythmic movements and vibrant costumes, students will embark on a journey that celebrates the heritage and history of members of the Korean ethnic group in Jilin and other provinces of north-eastern China. This program provides a hands-on opportunity for students to engage with cross-cultural traditions in a supportive and inclusive environment. With dance inspired by the motions of farming such as ‘walking the field ridges,’ participants will learn the significance behind each movement, fostering cultural awareness and empathy. Chinese Korean Ethnic Dance aims to ignite curiosity and foster connections, creating an unforgettable experience that not only educates but also inspires a deep appreciation for cultural diversity.

A child-friendly take on our popular Aboriginal Culture for a Day, our Mini Aboriginal Cultural Day is tailored to Early Childhood and immerses children in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures through the following 3 workshops: Aboriginal Dance & Didgeridoo Aboriginal Storytelling & Artefacts Aboriginal Symbolic Art Each workshop will run for 30-minutes, and this experience is tailored to your centre’s schedule. The Mini Aboriginal Cultural Day experience is priced at $1350 + GST and can accommodate up to 40 children. (This experience is valued at $499 + GST per session for a total of $1497 + GST, making it a more cost-effective option for children to explore a variety of cultural aspects).

Hip Hop Lyric Writing is a program where creativity and expression collide! This immersive experience invites students to explore the ins and outs of hip-hop culture in an engaging and interactive setting. By introducing students to the vibrant world of hip hop, and through a series of exercises, students are guided through the process of transforming their ideas into hip-hop verses. Step by step, students learn to break down their thoughts into lyricism, igniting their curiosity and enthusiasm.
Our First Nations Presenters across Australia are available to provide: Acknowledgement of Country Smoking Ceremony Didgeridoo and Dance Performances

Program_Name: Embedding Aboriginal Perspectives in the Workplace
Description: This professional development session led by Victorian Aboriginal Elder from Palawa Country, Aunty Gabby, supports professionals in respectfully integrating Aboriginal perspectives into their work. Through storytelling, discussion, and reflection, participants gain insights into the importance of positive reconciliation and honouring First Nations voices.

Uncle Paul, a respected Wakka Wakka Elder, shares his passion for traditional arts and cultural knowledge through captivating storytelling. Participants will learn about Aboriginal culture as a living heritage, fostering mutual understanding and respect.

Discover the rich history and significance of Aboriginal art through a hands-on workshop led by Victorian Aboriginal Elder and artist from Palawa Country, Aunty Gabby. Participants will engage with traditional Aboriginal symbols and art techniques on gum leaves, with the option to conjoin their creations into an artwork memento of the experience to display in the office. This workshop creates an open environment for discussion on broader topics surrounding Aboriginal art, culture and traditions.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Korean Classical Dance engages your students in the sights and sounds of enduring art forms from Korea! Tracing back 5000 years ago to its Shamanistic origins, this engaging program offers a captivating introduction to traditional Korean and folk dances, exploring the culture and history behind these mesmerising forms of expression. Students will actively participate in this interactive program, immersing themselves in movement and dance. Guided by the presenter, they will learn to emulate traditional dance variations like fan, long sleeve, and drum dances, and even have the opportunity to wear pieces of traditional attire!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Our Mime Magnifique! program is filled with action, fun and festivities. Taking participants on a journey exploring French culture and history, they will learn the significance of the French artform of mime. With charades, magic tricks, and more, the presenter brings theatre to life in a highly interactive and engaging workshop.

Japanese calligraphy, also known as Shodo, is one of the oldest and most profound traditional art forms in Japan. In this program, an experienced Shodo artist will introduce the history and origins of calligraphy. Through this program, participants can further explore Shodo by learning various brush techniques, calligraphy styles, stroke order, and the balance of Japanese characters.

Japanese Ink Painting, also known as Sumi-e, guides participants in preparing inks and incorporating different ink tones and brush techniques to create traditional ink paintings. By capturing objects from nature through their individual interpretations and expressing themselves through the art, participants can experience traditional Japanese ink paintings, and the exploration of the inner self through this meditative session.

Our Aboriginal Storytelling and Artefacts program combines storytelling, artefacts and interactive activities, creating an engaging session for your students! During the session, students will learn about different aspects of Aboriginal culture through storytelling, as well as an introduction to the history of Aboriginal tools and artefacts. Further activities such as acting out stories and engaging with cultural artefacts give the students the opportunity to further immerse themselves in Aboriginal culture throughout this program.

Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, SA, VIC, WA
Genre: Dance, Languages, Martial Arts, Music, Science, Storytelling, Sustainability, Theatre, Visual Arts, Wellbeing
Description: This program allows the choice of 3 individual pre-primary programs. You can explore one culture, language or topic in depth or travel the world with a program from each continent. Each workshop will run for 30-minutes, and this experience is tailored to your centre’s schedule. Once the programs are finalised, you will receive a personalised timetable to ensure the day runs smoothly. The Mini Multicultural Day experience is priced at $1350 + GST and can accommodate up to 40 children. (This experience is valued at $499 + GST per session for a total of $1497 + GST, making it a more cost-effective option for children to explore a variety of cultural programs). Please note, not all pre-primary programs are available as part of this experience.

Aria award winner, songbird and folkloric explorer Kavisha is known for her humour, poetry, and spirituality. Singing in English and Italian, she will take you on a journey through time and space, exploring over 600 years of Italian folk music. Songs of the field, love, birth, and protest; Kavisha delves into how people expressed their lives through song and how these styles differ between region, time, and language.

Le Voce Delle Luna, The Voice of the Moon Choir sings a vibrant blend of traditional and contemporary Italian folk songs with a passion and enthusiasm that is infectious. A vibrant group of women, Le Voce Della Luna present traditional folk songs sung from their hearts with passion and enthusiasm. The aim of this remarkable showcase of mothers, wives and sisters is to retain and promote the Italian heritage, culture, arts and traditions through music and song.

Program_Name: Introducing Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) in Education
Description: This live session will provide an introduction to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), and apply its principles, practices and challenges to educational settings. The facilitator will provide teachers with new ideas and perspectives to ensure students feel represented, valued and included in the classroom. This will take an interactive format including lecture slides, activities, practical resources and engaging discussion. By fostering a safe and open environment for students, they will develop their critical and creative thinking and be empowered to reach their full potential.

Program_Name: Introduction to Embedding Aboriginal Perspectives in the Classroom
Description: Aligned with the Cross Curriculum priority in the Australian Curriculum of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures, this session will introduce teachers/educators to how they can respectfully and appropriately teach this area of study. Co-facilitated by a First Nations presenter, the session will foster a safe and inclusive environment built on mutual respect and intercultural understanding. By engaging in the stories, knowledge, histories and experiences of First Nations peoples, and learning from one another, participants will begin a journey of ongoing and meaningful engagement. The key objective of the session is to inspire reflection and critical thinking and provide important perspectives to honour First Nations voices in the classroom.

Designed to support teachers in addressing the Intercultural Capability component of the Australian Curriculum, this live session will provide teachers and educators with the necessary tools to create inclusive and culturally responsive learning environments for students. With its interactive format, including lecture slides, activities, practical resources and engaging discussion, teachers will gain invaluable skills and knowledge to prepare students for our increasingly interconnected world.

Journey alongside a mesmerising travelling belly dancer! She finds a drum, a sword and a magnificent pair of golden wings in a battered old suitcase. Discover how these objects unlock the secrets of Ancient and modern Egypt, in an engaging music and dance adventure. This program is also available as Magical Wings of Ancient Egypt for a pre-primary audience.

In this pre-primary adaption of Ticket to Cairo! uncover the enchantment of the Magical Wings of Ancient Egypt. Students experience the beauty of the mesmerising theatrical wings, crafted from shimmering metallic fabric, supported by two hand-held sticks. Participants will love learning the easy-to-follow Egyptian dances and twirling their wings to the enchanting rhythms and melodies of The Middle East, creating an array of swirling colours!

Multicultural Moves is a unique interactive program that engages students in popular dance styles from around the world. In this program, students will learn the basic moves of various dance styles such as Jamaican Dancehall, Afro Dance, and Hip-Hop. The presenters will also introduce students to the historical and cultural perspectives and significance of these dances. Multicultural Moves offers tools that go beyond just artistic expression and performance to also support students’ mental wellbeing and improve their social skills and teamwork.

Filipino Music and Storytelling is a captivating program where Filipino language and culture come to life. In this program, students will experience uniquely narrated stories, where they get to jump in oral tales and leap into songs and movements! The presenter also uses ukulele, props, and Kamishibai (paper theatre) to engage students in a celebration of Filipino community, culture, and stories.

Zumba is an exciting and energetic celebration of culture, incorporating popular international music and modern beats. Zumba is a Latin-inspired total-body workout designed to create a dynamic and fun fitness routine. Our Zumba, Beats and Culture program is modified according to age-appropriate intensities with easy-to-follow moves and tunes. Students will learn a mix of low and high-intensity, interval-style moves, which will increase their coordination and boost their mood. The presenter will also introduce students to various cultures, music, and dance styles from around the world including Latin America, Africa, India, and Turkey.

Chinese Instrumental Duet is an excellent introduction to Chinese classical music. Exploring various Chinese musical styles and songs, the presenters will engage with traditional Chinese instruments, including wind instruments like the dizi (Chinese flute) and bow instruments like the Erhu (Chinese two-stringed vertical violin).

Africa meets the middle east is an engaging program that explores the musical traditions of both regions. The session highlights the similarities and differences between African and Middle Eastern rhythms, instruments, and beats, offering students the opportunity to learn about the key elements that shape different music styles. Delving into sounds and rhythms from both regions, this program will foster a deeper understanding of how music reflects cultural and historical significance. Students will also explore the connections and distinctions between the musical traditions of Africa and the Middle East, gaining a greater appreciation for their shared influences and unique qualities.

Beats around the World is a multicultural percussion program that aims to encourage rhythmic awareness and share different beats, grooves, and rhythms from various parts of the world. Students will explore multicultural beats from the Middle East, Turkey, Balkans, Latin America, India, and Africa. The presenter will share stories from his global journeys and musical encounters. What makes this program special is the eclectic combination of world percussion in one comprehensive session.

Turkish music is influenced by the country’s Turkic, Byzantine, and Ottoman heritage, in addition to its proximity to an intersection of cultures from across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. Turkish Rhythms explores Turkish culture using music and dance. Through the beats of the Darbuka, students will learn about the rhythmical elements of percussion such as timing, and experience dances and stories

Didgeridoo, Beats and Culture is the perfect introduction to the world’s oldest living culture. The presenter, Ganga, is a descendant of the Palawa people of Tasmania, who fuses this ancient instrument with electronic production and vocals and has presented around the world. Participants will engage with traditional musical instruments, storytelling, and hands-on activities, gaining a deeper appreciation for the world’s oldest living culture.

Fans are an integral part of Chinese lifestyle and are important artefacts in Chinese history and culture. In this workshop, participants will have the opportunity to decorate paper panels of the folding fan, providing a blank canvas to express their creativity.

In our Timorese Infusion workshop, three musicians with roots in Timor-Leste, singer Paulo, guitarist Gil, and percussionist Zeca, play traditional Timorese songs and highlight their historical influences. Featuring music, drumming, and stories, this Timorese trio draw from their rich musical heritage and share their experiences living in Timor-Leste.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: In Opa! Greek Dance and Culture, a highly interactive program, children will explore Greek culture and history through traditional music, dance, and storytelling. Children will have the opportunity to participate in the Zorba dance and listen to Greek mythologies and folk songs. They will also be introduced to authentic instruments such as the Baglama, Tzoura and the Cretan Lyra. *This program will be touring NSW during May 2025!

Traditionally used as a weapon and a tool for hunting, digging and ceremonies, the Boomerang is created to come back to the person who throws it. By incorporating the cultural significance of the tool, students will learn how and why it is important to engage in safe Boomerang practice and will have the opportunity to use specially designed safe Boomerangs. With this active and educational program, Boomerang Throwing allows students to develop an appreciation for an important aspect of Indigenous culture. As Boomerang Throwing is an outdoor program, our other activity-based program, Indigenous Games can be offered as a wet weather option.

Aboriginal Games is a highly interactive, activity-based program that has been developed to simulate early Aboriginal Australian life experiences. Aboriginal Games provides students with an engaging way to imitate hunting, fishing and gathering, and provides important cultural understandings. All of the materials and resources used within the program are safe alternatives for the real objects. Aboriginal Games can be held indoors/outdoors, depending on weather conditions, and is only suitable to be held in a wide open area, such as a gym or oval.

Dancing around India, a highly educational and interactive program engages students with diverse aspects of Indian culture. Students discover folk dances from the four regions of the Indian Subcontinent – North, South, East and West and develop a deeper understanding and awareness of the regional cultural differences. Dancing around India helps students to understand why each dance holds cultural significance through the exploration of food, festivals and landmarks from each region. To conclude, students will have the opportunity present their dances in costume!

Well-renowned performer Chris brings the delight of the holidays to you with his Christmas “Elf Christo” special. “Elf Christo” is a fun character with lots of Christmas spirit, helping children appreciate the history, customs and traditions of Christmas. A December exclusive, perfect for engaging young children, this magical and interactive Christmas program is brimming with storytelling, juggling and balloon bending.

Commedia dell’arte began in the 16th century in Italy and its mask theatre became the basis for modern-day comedy and clowning! This Commedia dell’arte solo show introduces the audience to well-known historic Commedia characters such as Pantalone, the grumpy mayor, and the know-it-all il Dottore. Using music, mime, magic and mayhem, Commedia dell’arte is presented as a clowning show full of energy, fun and silliness! This program details the masks themselves, the characterisation of the Commedia characters, and encourages audience participation and circus skills. Commedia dell’arte is a show that all ages can enjoy! *Adaptable to suit pre-primary and lower primary age groups*

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Acclaimed singer and dancer Seble shares the rich diversity of Ethiopian culture to learners of all ages with her highly interactive workshops. In Ethiopian Dance and Culture, Seble will share songs, dance moves and stories from her home country, and from her travels around the world from a very young age with the Ethiopian Circus.

Peter and Marie have been playing live music together since 1969. In Classic French Music they are joined by French cabaret singer Corrine, to present classics of early 20th century Paris. The trio play music from Edith Piaf, Django Reinhardt, Sidney Bechet and Jaqueline Baker and contextualizes the music by introducing the lyrics, instruments and cultural context in French and English according to the student’s level.

Egyptian Rhythms and Dance explores Egyptian culture through dance, music and engaging discussion. Students will learn about the cultural significance of regional dances, and the evolution of social folk dance to stage performance. Through percussive instruments and body percussion, students will experience a range of Folkloric dance styles and rhythms from across Egypt. Older students can also delve into the issues of Orientalism and the Western ‘mythstory’ surrounding bellydance (Raks Sharqi). This highly interactive and engaging program can be tailored to suit different age groups.

In Vietnamese Classical Music, the presenter will introduce learners to the T’rung (ancient Vietnamese bamboo xylophone) and an assortment of other traditional instruments, through performance, cultural stories, and interactivity! The participants will be exposed to these impressive instruments as they give voice to the beauty of Vietnamese Classical Music and traditions.

Using brush strokes and painted characters, Chinese Calligraphy & Brush Ink Painting, an interactive workshop focuses on imagery and self-expression. Originating from the year 618, students will learn and explore the significance of Chinese Calligraphy & Brush Ink Painting in Chinese culture.

Brazilian Drumming is a loud and fabulous introduction to Brazilian culture! The presenters will introduce the history, rhythms and culture of Brazil including Carnival and the famous Olodum drumming group. Presenters will provide metal buckets for the students so they can learn how to drum. They will be taught various Brazilian rhythms in this Brazilian Drumming workshop.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Predominantly performed during Lunar New Year and Mid-Autumn Festival, Vietnamese Classical Dance has been an innate part of Vietnamese culture since ancient times; dating as far back as 600BCE! Traditional dance in Vietnam represent the harmony of Vietnamese cultures and the people, and can take many forms such as: Fan Dance Hat Dance Lotus Flower Dance Umbrella Dance Featuring great skill, traditional dress, and a colourful performance, Vietnamese Classical Dance will have participants amazed at the sight before them.

Join Dean Frenkel – renowned storyteller, social scientist, and Guinness World Record holder – on an uplifting musical and cultural journey tracing the origins of the didgeridoo back to its scientifically verified birthplace in Australia. In this unique performance, Dean weaves together ancient creation stories, indigenous vocal traditions, and interactive musical demonstrations. The journey moves from Arnhem Land to India, then onward to Siberia, interconnecting global traditions like throat singing, chanting, whistling, and the deep, resonant tones of the didgeridoo. Dean is internationally respected for his mastery of indigenous sound techniques. He was endorsed by the late Djalu Gurriwiwi, the globally revered Yolngu musician and spiritual figure. Dean’s background in anthropology and his work as a social scientist enrich his storytelling with cultural insight and historical depth.

Latin American Dance introduces students to dances such as Salsa, Cha Cha Cha, Merengue, Bachata and Tango. Latin American Dance explores the history and cultural significance of dance in Latin America. Presenters will use upbeat music and can incorporate the Spanish language as they describe their personal experiences of Latin American cultures. **This workshop can be offered as a solo dancing class or a partner dancing class.

Chinese Ribbon dance is a traditional art form that originated in the Han and Tang Dynasties. Chinese Ribbon Dance is comprised of long flowing ribbons and choreography to synchronised traditional Chinese music, the audience will be amazed at the colourful and captivating demonstration, and will get the chance to try it themselves!

An ancient form of folk dance first documented in the Eastern Han Dynasty, Chinese Lantern Dance dates back 2,000 years ago and is used to tell stories and traditions of Chinese Culture. Originally used for light and worship, the Lantern has become a symbol of prosperity and honouring ancestors.

Babushka’s Spanish Fiesta workshop introduces students to Spanish culture and follows with choreographed dance and folkloric music, inspired by the famous Spanish dance – Flamenco. In Spanish Fiesta, students will begin to explore Spanish culture through this colourful, vibrant and interactive program.

Australian Indigenous communities have long understood the importance of sustainability with traditional knowledge passed down through generations. This practical workshop, Caring for Country allows students to learn about Indigenous sustainability practices including bushfire prevention using fire-stick farming, bush tucker, and predicting rain just by the squawking of the Cockatoo. Through respecting and understanding our environment, we can conserve our earth, respect our wildlife and reduce our carbon footprint – vital for the well-being of future generations.

Aboriginal Storytelling through Art is a practical workshop where the presenter will invite the students to learn Aboriginal art symbols for man, woman, child, the land and numerous animals. The presenter creates a story using the symbols and explains how to interpret it to the students. After copying and practising drawing the symbols, the students will get to create and draw their own story (with the presenter’s assistance) using the symbols and techniques they have learned. Aboriginal Storytelling through Art invites students to present their stories to the rest of the group. The cultural experience represents Aboriginal art in a fun and unique way, allowing for a perfect intercultural experience at any age.

With 20 years of experience as a variety entertainer, travelling across the globe, multi-talented and well-renowned Man of a Million Faces, Chris, brings his own unique style to cultural education. With the choice between a French or Italian-inspired theatre workshop, Chris’ Man of a Million Faces sparks interest in culture, cuisine, language, landmarks and history through the following: Theatre art including Commedia dell’arte Theatre magic Mime art, charades and puppetry with colourful characters Leather mask making

Our July exclusive, Bastille Day with Chris is filled with action, fun and festivities. Renowned variety performer Chris takes students on a journey exploring the culture, history and significance of the French national holiday, Bastille Day. With puppetry, charades, magic tricks, juggling and more, Bastille Day with Chris brings history to life in a highly interactive and engaging workshop. This incursion provides the perfect way to celebrate Bastille Day!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Polynesian Infusion takes participants on a journey to the Islands with its energetic and enthusiastic performance and interactive workshops. Through a fast-paced combination of music, dance, storytelling and craft, participants will come to know and appreciate the ancient and fascinating cultures of the Pacific. Polynesian Infusion’s talented performers are skilled in a wide variety of musical traditions including drums, ukelele and chanting. Participants will be presented with a traditional dance performance and engaged further with a Hula lesson.

Signifying good fortune, prosperity and longevity, the Lion Dance is an art form dating back to the 12th century and is an important part of the Chinese Celebration of the Lunar New Year! Little Lion Dance is a highly colourful and engaging experience that will have young children excited to see the lions up close, learn about the origins, and interact with the presenters!

In Les Chansons Françaises, Pauline shares stories of her Parisienne childhood in an interactive vocal session with songs that explore intercultural understanding. Depending on the age group Pauline will teach students a popular children’s song or a catchy chorus from the Yé-Yé era of the 1960s which they’ll sing accompanied by the band. Students will hear and speak French throughout Les Chansons Françaises and end the session learning to waltz!

Born in France to French and Sephardic-Moroccan parents Pauline Maudy teaches Jewish Sephardic songs with influences from Turkey, Greece and the Balkans reflecting the widespread geography of the diaspora.inFolkloric to Flamenco, John, a Flamenco guitarist, will accompany the songs and teach ‘palmas’, the clapping that is a common accompaniment to Flamenco music. Folkloric to Flamenco can be tailored to Spanish language students.

Nepalese-born Dheeraj is recognised as the foremost Tabla player in Australia. The Tabla is the quintessential percussion instrument of the Indian subcontinent and one of the most complicated drums to play. The Nepalese percussion instrument, the Madal, is the backbone of Nepalese folk music and is often played while hiking in the mountains of the Himalayas! in Rhythm of Nepal, Dheeraj will demonstrate Nepalese-Indian rhythms and hip-hop vocal percussion. He will also introduce the fastest percussion instrument in the world – the Tabla!

Songs of Uganda is a workshop from Joseph that centres around his heritage from the Baganda tribe in Uganda. He begins by performing traditional songs in the Baganda language accompanied by the Bakisimba dance and Kidigida rhythms. Students accompany Joseph by singing and learning the rhythms and Songs of Uganda. Instruments used include Engoma (drums), Endingidi (tube fiddle), Amadinda (xylophone) and Adungu (harp).

Program_Name: Wayang Kulit with Sofari and Tom
Description: Presented by Tom and Sofari, the Wayang Kulit, is a puppetry performance using traditional hand-carved shadow puppets from Java, Indonesia! The Indonesian words wayang (shadow or ghost) and kulit (leather or skin) define the two-dimensional Puppets that are flat, translucent figures cut out from leather and projected against a screen. The mystical manipulation between the light and screen creates a ‘living’ silhouette, and theatrical storytelling brings to life the ancestral spirits which are said to dwell within the puppets. The Climactic scenes in Wayang Kulit with Sofari and Tom are based on Hindu epics such as the Ramayama cycle. Find out about Indonesian characters and community through this compelling and ghostly medium.

Le Gioie Delle Donne, The Joys of the Women Italian Choir sing joyous folk songs from all regions of Italy. The choir is very proud to keep the Italian culture and heritage alive by sharing a rich and diverse repertoire of songs and music from Italy’s vibrant traditions. Through song, the choir brings to life the warmth of Italian traditions, fostering connection and joy among audiences.

The Mbira, sometimes called the ‘thumb piano’ is an African instrument. It has been played by the Shona people of Zimbabwe for over a thousand years! In Mbira of Zimbabwe, George Joe will introduce its origins and history before playing the Mbira and singing some traditional tunes in the Shona language which students will accompany with percussion and singing.

A child-friendly take on our popular Chinese Martial Arts program, Mini Martial Arts is a highly interactive, fun, and exciting program, ideal for young children under 6. A typical workshop explores the origins and characteristics that Martial Arts is known for; and aims to teach an appreciation of the mind, body, and spirit, through engaging and meaningful activities. Mini Martial Arts can be adapted to different ages and physical abilities, the children will have the opportunity to try out some simple movements and actions for themselves!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Indonesian Infusion will take participants on an immersive and interactive journey, showcasing the amazing diversity of the Indonesian community. Through customs, language, dance, traditional dress and music, the presenters explore the islands of Sumatra, Java, Bali and more. This colourful Indonesian Infusion program will give audiences an appreciation and insight into Indonesian culture!

Colombian musician Hugo Salcedo teams with Latin dance instructor Julia Gonzalez to present this fun introduction to Latin dance styles like Salsa, Bachata and Brazilian Samba in Latino Grooves! Using traditional as well as contemporary instruments, the duo provide an energetic and insightful music and dance program and can incorporate Spanish language to suit the level of students.

Explore the unique and vibrant culture of Naples in Italy in Bella Italia! Napoli native Mira takes students through her childhood to learn about this ancient city. In Bella Italia, students will sing along to Neapolitan folk songs and practice traditional folk dances. The Italian language level can be adjusted to the ability of the students.

In this interactive Music of Southern Italy workshop, students will discover the rhythms and sounds of the traditional music styles of southern Italy. The castanettes, the diatonic accordion, the tamburello, the putipu and the ciaramella are some of the instruments that bring energy and melody to this program! Then, with the infectious live music backing them, students will practice the lively folk dance the Tarantella.

Join Rowan for an incredible performance of high-energy, intricate Bavarian folk dances in Tirol Dancing! He will demonstrate various German and Austrian traditional dances such as the Waltz, Polka and Zwiefacher. Students will also have the chance to learn how to do the energetic Schuhplattler– the famous German slap dance. MUSIC – Learning balance, space awareness, coordination – Value dance works from Australia and other societies, cultures and times – Recognise differences in dance works from different times, cultures and societies. SOCIETY & ENVIRONMENT – Ensure that schooling contributes to a socially cohesive society that respects and appreciates cultural, social and religious diversity – Students interact with people and cultures other than their own and are equipped to contribute to the global community. LOTE – Intercultural knowledge and language awareness – Develop an understanding of some of the differences in how people eat and dress, sign and gesture, write and say things – Inspires interest in and respect for other cultures.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: In Viva Mexico – A Cultural Journey, our presenter performs with instruments including the Mexican harp, Mexican and Spanish guitars, violin and trumpet. Students will learn folk dances and the meaning of Spanish lyrics found in La Bamba and other popular songs. The presenter will explain the cultural history of the instruments and the Charro suit worn by the Mariachis.

In Hip-Hop Infusion, the high-energy interactive program, students will discover the significance of hip-hop and urban dance culture around the world. Using a variety of super-danceable beats, our presenters will create an atmosphere that will have all students up and dancing. Hip-Hop Infusion is the perfect introduction to the expressive, powerful world of hip-hop!

The Sound of Multicultural Australia Trio is a combination of ancient melodies and African rhythms woven into compositions that can only be found in Australia. The Trio comprises Uygu, a world-renowned musician, Yaw, Ghanian elder and percussionist, and Richard, who invites the musicians to share their culture.

Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, VIC, Virtual, WA
Description: Aboriginal Infusion is the perfect introduction to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories and cultures. Students will develop an understanding of the rich and ancient traditions of Australia’s first inhabitants. Aboriginal Infusion is a highly interactive and engaging program that enables students to explore different cultural aspects such as Dance and Didgeridoo, Aboriginal Artefacts and Storytelling. Please note: the exact cultural aspects explored in this program will depend on the presenter’s area/s of specialisation.

In Riding the Waves, Venezuelan engineer Ramileth demonstrates the science of telecommunications with experiments in sound and light waves and the electromagnetic spectrum! This program will help students understand how everyday technology like mobile phones actually work – as well as give students insight into what a career in engineering involves. This Science Communicator program is part of a series of school incursions developed to highlight the underpinning role that culture plays in shaping human progress, presented in partnership with the Royal Society of Victoria.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Immerse your students in the culture of ancient India that is still practised to this day in the workshop Classical Indian Dance. After a fantastic performance set to the sound of classical instruments and Sanskrit chants, students will learn some of the symbolic gestures and movements and the stories they tell.
A symbol of beauty and grace, Chinese Fan Dance is a colourful captivating workshop that will get students moving with their own fans as they learn all about the Chinese Fan Dance and its origins.

Genre: Dance, Martial Arts, Music, Visual Arts
Description: Chinese Culture for a Day incorporates two rotating sessions into one all-day program celebrating diversity in Chinese culture. Our presenters can tailor Chinese Culture for a Day to include Chinese Lion Dance, Martial Arts, a drumming workshop, folk dancing, calligraphy or lantern making.

From laidback melodies to exciting dance beats, this program introduces students to the musical sounds of the Caribbean and to soca, calypso and reggae music played on their national instrument; the steel drums.

Bali in Motion provides students with the opportunity to experience a true taste of Balinese Cultural activities! Music, dance and the visual arts form a foundation for traditional Balinese life, and myths and legends are incorporated into these arts. In Bali in Motion, your students will participate in a colourful and interactive program, and gain an appreciation for the harmony within the culture.

Embark on a musical journey to Southeastern Europe with an interactive music program suitable for all ages. In Balkan Beats, students can use whatever percussion instruments they have available – Darabuka, Djembe, Bendir, or just clap their hands! As they learn the rhythms of the Turkish and Bulgarian dancers and Macedonian maestros.

Fairytale Puppetry – Exploring Languages engages students with language and culture through a range of nine classic fairytales and stories told through exquisitely crafted traditional European hand puppets. Fairytale Puppetry features audience participation and are available in French and Mandarin. This program can be tailored to suit different ages or language levels. The Jungle Book: – 45 minutes – Pre-Primary and Primary – French, Mandarin, Italian, German, Spanish, Indonesian, Japanese The performance and language content (LOTE) is adapted accordingly. The level of vocabulary is easy. The children will be asked to sing and repeat easy words in the language they are learning. Ideal show for beginners. Cinderella – 50 minutes –Years Prep – Year 8 – French, Italian, German, Spanish The performance and language content (LOTE) is adapted accordingly. The level of vocabulary is for students who have a reasonable understanding of the language. The puppets will interact with the students, in the language, they are learning. Ideal show for students who have done a minimum of 1 to 2 years of LOTE.

Yoga and Mindfulness engages participants in this ancient practice that uses breathing, flexibility, and strength to boost mental and physical wellbeing. The presenter will share the symbolism and cultural history of yoga, flowing yoga postures, classical hand gestures, meditation and breath techniques that are tailored to all ages and abilities.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: An art form that emerged from enslaved Africans in Brazil, disguising their fight into a dance, Capoeira has evolved to become one of the most fascinating combination of dance and martial arts movements in the world. An endangered art form, Cool Capoeira introduces the history and evolution to its special protected status as intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO. You will be able to learn and experience rhythmic acrobatic manoeuvres accompanied by the beautiful sound of the Berimbau, an African instrument – the heartbeat of this dynamic performance. Capoeira is for all, whether you are more of an acrobat, a musician, a singer, a dancer or a martial artist, some aspect of Cool Capoeira will speak to you. As a famous Capoeira master, Mestre Canjiquinha, always said “Capoeira does not have creed, does not have colour, does not have flag, it is from the people, it will run through the world”.

Aboriginal Culture For A Day immerses your students in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures with three rotating sessions of cultural programs led by an experienced team of presenters. The Aboriginal Culture For A Day program can include the following sessions: Art and Storytelling Culture and history Dreamtime Stories Artefacts Boomerang throwing Dance and Singing (with Didgeridoo) Mindfulness through Didgeridoo Please note, individual sessions will be dependent upon factors such as presenter availability, participant numbers, space/ set-up requirements and weather conditions.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: In Japanese Infusion, the presenter brings Japanese culture to life with this beautifully crafted program. They teach children about Japanese culture, traditions, seasons and celebrations through the use of songs, games and storytelling. Japanese Infusion is an active and engaging program that will have students learning words and numbers in Japanese and, most importantly, having lots of fun.

Let’s Kung Fu with Panda is perfect for younger students. Highly interactive, Let’s Kung Fu with Panda includes a traditional Kung Fu demonstration, Tai-chi, fan dance and the ancient sword dance! Students will then meet Panda who will do a fun Kung Fu workshop with them. Suitable for years prep – 2.

Derived from Mongolian folk religion and the legend of the Shaman, Bukhu, the Mongolian Throat Singer presents traditional throat singing from his homeland. Alongside the Mongolian horse-head fiddle, the singing is skillfully crafted into an exciting and engaging performance using contemporary loop pedals and modern beats!

Robin Zirwanda is a native of Iraq, where his people, the Assyrians, have lived for 7000 years. Presenting this program with his teenage son Josh, they introduce the Assyrian culture through catchy songs in the Assyrian Aramaic language (yes, they speak the language Jesus spoke!). They explore themes of symbolism, cultural practice, displacement and assimilation, demonstrating traditional rhythms, and showing how music has evolved. Their vibrant costumes, based on the dress of their ancient royal ancestors, serve as a talking point to connect their ancient Assyrian heritage with our modern community.

Rebetika – The Greek Blues presents Rebetika music created when the Ottoman, Byzantine and Greek worlds came together through urban subcultures in 20th-century Greece. The lyrics tell stories spanning love, loss, refugee tales and the trials of everyday life played on guitar-like instruments such as the Bouzouki – hence the nickname ‘The Greek Blues’!

Rhythm Empire is a theatrical multicultural music and dance extravaganza featuring rhythms, dances, instruments, language and costumes from across the ancient world. The colourful history and cultures of the Silk Road and the Middle East come to life when audiences join the performance in Rhythm Empire, to barter, trade, and perform in a rollicking world music jam!

Program_Name: Hero Ladybirds of the Galapagos Islands
Description: Carolina Zuluaga is an ecologist who worked on the project to introduce the Australian Ladybird of the Galapagos Islands with the aim of controlling a feral insect that was destroying the balance in the ecosystem. Through her firsthand experience and the help of cute hand puppets, she tells a fabulously quirky story that helps children understand basic ecology. This Science Communicator program is part of a series of school incursions developed to highlight the underpinning role that culture plays in shaping human progress, presented in partnership with the Royal Society of Victoria.

Fire of Flamenco incorporates dance, music and singing and has a rich, multicultural history influenced by Roma, Arab, West African and Spanish cultures. The music is created with instrumental guitar, unique vocals, clapping rhythms and another percussion. In Fire of Flamenco, students will have to opportunity to try the accompanying ‘palmas’ and learn some of the dance moves for themselves.

The Cajon originated in Africa, then travelled to South America, Asia and Europe – it’s a truly global instrument! Tawanda is an expert Cajon maker and percussionist and presents this cajon drumming workshop where students will try different styles of Cajon Drumming and hear how migration and being open to change can lead to innovation and new shared meaning.

Hailed by parents and teachers as a one-woman-multicultural-rock-concert-for-kids, Jungle Shimmy is a dynamic music and dance adventure across the world! With colourful props and fun, easy-to-follow dances including Belly Dance, Bollywood, Bhangra, Turkish, Egyptian, Gulf, and Lebanese folk styles, everybody is up on their feet dancing. Jungle Shimmy’s shrill cry of a Zaghareet, Middle Eastern instruments and rhythms like Khaleegi, Maqsoum and Beledi, and unique handmade puppet theatre draw audiences of all ages into a captivating world of culture and creative self-expression.

Iranian Voices features the voices of women from Iran and the Iranian diaspora. Iranian-Australian musician Gelareh Pour will present stories and cultures of musicians in Iran through the exploration of Iranian women singers before and after the 1979 Revolution in Iran. Throughout the storytelling, Gelareh plays the Kamancheh, a fascinating and ancient Iranian string instrument which is an ancestor of the European violin.

Indian Instrumental Infusion engages participants with Indian classical and contemporary music through significant instruments, including the tabla and bansuri. The program is delivered by passionate musicians wholeheartedly committed to their art who share captivating sounds and rhythms from deeply rooted Indian classical music traditions.

Drumming and rhythm are an integral part of Middle Eastern Cultures and the foundation of Belly Dance. In Middle Eastern Drumming, students will experience vibrant and unique Middle Eastern rhythms and learn about their origin and influences. Atman will present several types of drums and instruments and students will try playing themselves.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Taiko Drumming, a traditional and original Japanese music program combines amazing performances and interactive workshops. Students are introduced to Japanese culture through music and language before the room shakes with the sound of the Taiko Drumming!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Chinese Classical Dance presents incredible performances of classical folk dances from across China, including the Lantern Dance, Ribbon Dance and Fan Dance. Participants will learn a short routine using some of the steps alongside traditional and contemporary Chinese music. The Chinese Classical Dance presenters will supply props such as ribbons, fans and lanterns for participants to dance with.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: In Music of the Andes, participants will explore the music and dances of the Inca culture from the Andes Mountains. Students will learn about traditional instruments and melodies that have been part of the Andes for generations. The session highlights the cultural significance of these instruments and their role in South American and Andean music, providing an opportunity to understand the region’s traditions and history.

Program_Name: The Tragic Genius of Mrs Einstein
Description: Albert Einstein is widely celebrated as the mind behind the Theory of Relativity – but did you know there was another brilliant physicist working with him? The Tragic Genius of Mrs Einstein, known as Mileva Maric, met Albert Einstein when they were both students in Zurich and together they conducted the experiments that would lead to E=mc2 and the Theory of Relativity. Using authentic letters between the couple, The Tragic Genius of Mrs. Einstein explores the human story behind the science.

Signifying good fortune, prosperity and longevity, the Chinese Lion Dance is an art form dating back to the 12th century! This Chinese Lion Dance workshop will give students an opportunity to see the Lion up close while gaining an insight into one of China’s oldest traditions and its cultural significance. This program is available as an educational workshop or performance and prices vary. Please enquire for more information.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Chinese Classical Music presents the origins of Chinese classical instruments and introduces traditional Chinese music. This is followed by a beautiful performance and an interactive workshop where participants learn a traditional song themselves.

Program_Name: Multicultural All Day or Half Day Program
Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, SA, VIC, WA
Genre: Dance, Languages, Martial Arts, Music, Science, Storytelling, Sustainability, Theatre, Visual Arts, Wellbeing
Description: Our Multicultural All Day or Half Day program allows a choice of three or five presenters and is tailored to suit your school bell times with a personalised timetable. Either explore one culture, language or topic in-depth or explore the world with a range of assorted programs. Students split into groups and rotate between 25-minute workshop sessions, then come together for a 50-minute interactive performance session to finish the day! To complement this program, we also offer free educational resources which explore the unit, ‘Exploring Diversity’, as well as lesson plans that provide extra activities and background context about the cultures being studied. With so many Cultural Presenters to choose from at Cultural Infusion, we can bring you an exciting and memorable day, which celebrates and shares understanding about diverse cultures! With 300 students or more, enquire about our All-Day program (choice of 5 presenters), and with 200 students or less, enquire about our Half-Day program (choice of 3 presenters).

Program_Name: Rhythms and Instruments of West Africa
Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, SA, VIC, WA
Description: In Rhythms and Instruments of West Africa, the musical cultures of West Africa are explored through rhythms and songs from Ghana, Guinea and Senegal. Students will be introduced to a range of instruments such as the djembe, dun dun drums, shekere, talking drum, balafon and more! Rhythms and Instruments of West Africa is an interactive program and students will be playing the drums and other percussion instruments.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: Middle Eastern Belly Dance introduces your audience to Arabic cultures through stories and movement. Participants get the chance to experience the beautiful, health-promoting movements of this highly expressive dance form. Participants are also introduced to the traditional significance and history of Middle Eastern Belly Dance in this lively and engaging program. Shimmies, undulations, and belly-pops are all part of the fun!

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Corporate, Pre Primary, Schools
Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, SA, VIC, WA
Description: Bollywood is an important part of modern Indian culture, referring to the Hindi film industry, and categorised by colourful displays of music, dance, and costume. Bollywood Infusion presents a vibrant workshop where participants will learn about the folk and classical origins of the Bollywood dances, the symbolism of some of the steps, and a short routine to Bollywood music.

Tailored_To: Assemblies & Events, Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Description: The earliest known drums in China date back to four thousand years ago! A performance of rhythm and colour, students will love this hands-on Chinese Drumming workshop as they drum out beats and learn about instruments behind the popular Lion Dance and Kung Fu soundtracks.

Available_In: ACT, NSW, QLD, SA, VIC, WA
Description: Martial arts, also traditionally known as wŭshù (武术) in Mandarin, are art forms dating back more than 4000 years ago. In Chinese Martial Arts, a high energy educational workshop, participants get to delve into the history and philosophy of martial arts in China as well as trying out different styles such as Tai-Chi for themselves. Directly translated as “acquired skill”, Kung-Fu refers to any discipline or skill obtained through hard work and practise, and is a concept of cultural significance that serves as the foundation for many martial arts. Able to be adapted to different ages and physical abilities, participants will develop an appreciation for the discipline, practice, and mastery that Chinese Martial Arts is famous for.
